mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds from a sharp weekly drop, weekday foot traffic and nearby purchases recover with a lag, pushing RETAIL_REC above its last-4-week average within four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above its prior 4-week average within 28 days after WORKPLACES stops falling and begins rising for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, more trips are delayed into local discretionary shopping, which raises RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks as people substitute neighborhood retail for longer commutes.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains at least 5 points above baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within 14 days while RESIDENTIAL remains at or above the stated threshold for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates more commuting and city-center activity, which lifts retail-and-recreation visits after about four weeks through stronger weekday and lunch-time demand.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days despite both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rising together from their current levels.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT stays below -35 while WORKPLACES also remains depressed, access costs and office-linked spending stay weak, so retail-and-recreation mobility falls further over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -35 for two consecutive weeks and WORKPLACES stays below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week mean within 28 days even though TRANSIT stays below -35 and WORKPLACES stays below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in PARKS mobility signals warmer-weather leisure substitution, and that outdoor activity spills into discretionary shopping, raising RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the week after a 10-point or larger weekly rise in PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM softens while RETAIL_REC is still below baseline, households are no longer concentrating trips on essentials, and discretionary retail catches up over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -3 after being near baseline for at least one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not move upward within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM drops below -3 from a near-baseline level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained move toward home-based activity, reflected by rising RESIDENTIAL and falling TRANSIT, reduces out-of-home discretionary shopping and keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds its prior 4-week average within 28 days even as RESIDENTIAL rises and TRANSIT falls.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS recovers sharply from a deep trough while TRANSIT remains weak, leisure demand is being redirected locally rather than into shopping districts, so RETAIL_REC stays lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 15 points from its prior week while TRANSIT stays below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week mean within 28 days despite PARKS rebounding and TRANSIT staying below -35.
